results.summary: ROVA - Roma CSOs promoting EU values
results.content: ROVA - Roma CSOs promoting EU values

beneficiaryAdministration:
The ROVA project launches its first call for proposals in 3 lots:

LOT 1: Call for proposals from individual civil society organisations registered and operating in Bulgaria, Czechia+Slovakia, Hungary, Romania, and Spain (available funding 300,000€ per country/country pair in the case of Czechia and Slovakia; max. grant per project 30,000€)

LOT 2: Call for proposals from individual NGOs registered and operating in other EU Member States (OTHER THAN Bulgaria, Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary, Romania, and Spain, available funding 200,000€ - max. grant per project 20,000€).

LOT 3: Call for proposals from national Roma coalitions from EU Member States (available funding 225,000€ - max grant per project 15,000€)


Submission process – calls for proposals from individual CSOs:

The application process consists of two stages: Concept notes and full proposals. The first round (submission of concept notes) is open until 5 pm CET on 5 August 2025.

Applications must be submitted by completing the the relevant online application form available on www.rovaproject.org.

During the application process applicants will be able to attend information sessions with the aim to help potential applicants to develop good project proposals, which will be advertised by national grant managing organisations. The dates are available in the detailed application guide.

Individual consultations will be offered to interested applicants. Info sessions are announced in the application guides and will be advertised by the intermediary organisations.

Applicants will be notified of the results of the first round of the competition no later than 9 September 2025. If shortlisted for the second round, they will receive an application form for the full proposal, which must be submitted no later than October 13 at 5 pm CET.

Funding decisions will be communicated no later than mid-November, and funding contracts will be concluded with successful applicants by 15 December 2025 at the latest.

Applications will be evaluated by external evaluators and a selection committee in both rounds.

For detailed application guides in national languages, including maximum funding amounts, expected number of grantees per country, eligibility criteria, eligible activities, selection and award criteria, visit www.rovaproject.org


Submission process – call for national coalitions:

The deadline for submitting detailed proposals is 5 pm CET on 5 August 2025.

Applications can only be submitted by completing the form available on the ROVA website (www.rovaproject.org)

We will hold online information sessions with the aim to help potential applicants to develop good project proposals. The information sessions will take place on:

  1. 26 June 2025, (11:00 CET)
  2. 6 July 2025 (11:00 CET)

Both sessions will have the same content. Individual consultations will be offered to interested applicants. See the application guide for the registration link.

Applicants will be informed about the selection results no later than 9 September 2025.

results.summary: Call for proposals for small grants 1/SPLOT/GM/2025
results.content: Call for proposals for small grants 1/SPLOT/GM/2025

beneficiaryAdministration:
Link to the application platform: http://siecsplot.pl/splot-wartosci/.

The value of the grant cannot be lower than EUR 2,500 or higher than EUR 7,500. No own contribution is required.

Objectives of the grant fund:

  1. strengthening the potential of civil society organisations and supported leaders to promote and protect EU values ​​and fundamental rights,
  2. strengthening the ability of supported organisations to represent the CSO sector and make effective decisions,
  3. increasing the presence of CSOs in public life and leaders in the forum of public debate,
  4. raising the level of involvement in law-making processes,
  5. strengthening the image of CSOs - a more favourable environment for civil society organisations,
  6. strengthening awareness of the importance of democratic values ​​for civil society and the role of organisations in their active promotion and protection.

The application is subject to a point assessment carried out by a team of experts gathered in the competition committee. Each application is assessed independently by 2 experts (experts sign an impartiality clause towards the assessed Grantee).

Subject criteria for grant projects

Grant projects submitted in the call must meet the following subject criteria:

Criterion 1 – The implementation of the grant project must relate to the priorities of the CERV programme - raising awareness of rights and values ​​by supporting civil society organisations; strengthening the protection and promotion of Union values, including respect for the rule of law; contributing to the implementation of democratic values, including by supporting dialogue, transparency and good governance, including in cases of shrinking space for civil society. Criterion verified on the basis of the Information contained in the application.

Criterion 2 - Implementation of the project exclusively in Poland. Fulfilment of this criterion is verified on the basis of the provisions in the application.

Criterion 3 – The value of the requested grant cannot be less than EUR 2,500 or more than EUR 7,500. Fulfilment of this criterion is verified on the basis of the provisions in the application.

Criterion 4 - Duration of the grant from 3 to 12 months. Grants in call no. 1/SPLOT/GM/2025 may be implemented in the period from December 1, 2025 to June 30, 2027. Fulfillment of this criterion is verified based on the application records.

Criterion 5 – Grant project settled using simplified methods based on results.

Criterion 6 – Project implemented by one entity.

Entities eligible to apply for a grant are independent civil society organisations registered in Poland, including organisations that:

  1. have their registered office in Poland,
  2. are non-profit (do not operate for profit),
  3. operate at local and/or regional and/or national level,
  4. respect fundamental rights and values ​​on which the EU is based,
  5. carry out activities in the areas covered by the CERV programme,
  6. are neither affiliated entities with the Grantor, nor have they been collaborators or contractors within 12 months prior to the date of application.

results.summary: Aspektus+ Regional Funding Program: Call 1) Hatókör and Call 2) Helyben ható
results.content: Aspektus+ Regional Funding Program: Call 1) Hatókör and Call 2) Helyben ható

beneficiaryAdministration:
Grants, knowledge sharing, networking – Aspektus+ is a complex four-year capacity building programme for rural NGOs in Hungary.

The sub-program “Hatókör” is for formal, independent, non-profit civil society organizations, established and operating in Hungary. The Hatókör programme is open to applications from organisations that have been operating for at least three years, have a total budget of more than HUF 25 million over the last three years and are independent of state and local government institutions.

The overall aim of this call is to support CSOs working in the countryside in Hungary (outside of the capital) to become more independent, stable and active agents of democracy and democratic values. Our goal is to help established CSOs to take the next step, to reach the next level of functioning. The grant aims to provide financial and professional support to intermediate CSOs, which could become potential new civil centres in the countryside, strengthening the cooperation and work of existing organisations with different skills/activities at regional level.

This grant is a core grant with a fixed amount of EUR 60 000. It can be used for the project goals (organizational development goals) and for operational costs. The grant will thus be used in three annual phases, in the form of a lump sum. Depending on the yearly evaluation and monitoring, the next year’s amount could be decreased.

The selection process will consist of two stages. In the first round of the application process, we will be seeking more detailed information on the organisation. In the second round, the applicants (maximum 32 short listed from 1st stage) will present their ideas for organisational development and capacity building. The final decision will be made by the evaluation committee consist of 12 members: the 4 external experts and 2 team members from each Aspect Group organization.

The sub-program “Helyben ható” is for formal, independent, non-profit civil society organizations, established and operating in the 4 core regions of Aspect Group (South Trans-Danubia, South Plains, North Plains, North Hungary). We are seeking to support established organisations who are engaged to take a next step towards independent, planned operations.

The overall aim of this call is to support CSOs working in the countryside in Hungary (outside of the capital) to become more independent, stable and active agents of democracy and democratic values. The form of the grant is a lump sum. It can be used mainly to cover the costs of capacity development and local community building programs. The grant amount for the 36-month program increases annually (in the first year fixed 6000 EUR, second year fixed 9000 EUR, third year fixed 15000 EUR) and the activities will be redesigned (if needed) after consultation.

“Helyben ható” is a two stage call. The first round of the application process is about eligibility, the organization and their project idea. The short listed organizations in the second stage must present a three-year project plan and elaborate in detail the goals, target group, program, activities, and budget plan. The final decision will be made by the evaluation committee consist of 12 members: the 4 external experts and 2 team members from each Aspect Group organization.

results.summary: Thematic grants
results.content: Thematic grants

beneficiaryAdministration:
The objective of the Call for thematic grants is to support:

• activities to ensure that groups at risk of discrimination, unequal treatment, hate speech and hate crimes (in particular LGBT+ people, women, people with disabilities, Roma, people with migration experience) enjoy the rights guaranteed by the Charter of Fundamental Rights; and

• evidence-based advocacy, watchdog and monitoring activities that support respect for the rule of law.

Total budget for the call: PLN 7 600 000 (approx. EUR 1 759 667) (Small thematic grants: PLN 2 600 000, approx. EUR 601 991; large thematic grants: PLN 5 000 000, approx. EUR 1 157 676).

Minimum/maximum grant amount:

• small grants up to PLN 50 000, plus an additional optional grant amount for organisation’s capacity building PLN 15 000 (which gives maximum total amount of PLN 65 000 – approx. EUR 15 050)

• large grants PLN 50 001 – PLN 100 000 plus an additional optional grant amount for organisation’s capacity building PLN 25 000 (which gives maximum total amount of PLN 125 000 – approx. EUR 28 942)

The thematic grants include a capacity building component in the form of an additional optional amount of funds earmarked for strengthening and developing the organisation, creating a stable basis for it to function further, drawing up strategy or forward-looking action and financial plans, and raising the standard of the organisation's work and management. The maximum amount of the capacity building grant is PLN 15 000 (approx. EUR 3 473) for small grants and PLN 25 000 (approx. EUR 5 789) for large grants.

In order to be eligible, applicants must:

• Be established in Poland.

• Be non-profit making and a civil society organisation.

• Respect EU values as laid down in Art.2 of the Treaty on European Union and the EU Charter of fundamental rights.

• Have eligible legal form:

o for large grants: foundations, associations registered in the National Court Register, church legal persons registered in the National Court Register, rural housewives’ circles, unions of associations

o for small grants: foundations, associations registered in the National Court Register, church legal persons registered in the National Court Register, rural housewives’ circles, unions of associations, so called ordinary associations

• Have been registered at least 12 months before submitting the application

• Have not been granted an institutional grant in Equal Rights Project grant scheme.

Only activities taking place in an EU Member State are eligible.

Submitted proposals will be evaluated in a one-stage process, by independent experts with knowledge and experience in the subject of the call.

results.summary: Call No. 1 for proposals for NGOs to participate in capacity building and receive financial support
results.content: Call No. 1 for proposals for NGOs to participate in capacity building and receive financial support

beneficiaryAdministration:
The objective of the call is to strengthen the capacity and resilience of regional grassroots CSOs to protect and promote EU values. The impact areas of the call include strengthened CSOs role to better integrate and promote EU values; increased capacity to influence policy and decision-making at various levels; more effective CSO operation and accountability to their target groups.

At the first stage of the call at least 40 regional CSOs in Lithuania will be selected to participate in the long-term comprehensive capacity building program NGO Leaders’ Academy. After successful graduation from the Academy, the CSOs will be invited to apply for project grants. At least 20 CSOs will be awarded project grants in the amount of up to EUR 30.000,-. The duration of the projects will be 10-12 months.

Eligibility requirements are as follows:

1. The applicant is an NGO established and operating in the Republic of Lithuania that meets the following definition: "A non-profit voluntary organization established as a legal entity, having a non-commercial purpose, independent of the local, regional and central government, public entities, political parties, and commercial organizations". Religious institutions, trade unions and political parties are not considered NGOs (this definition follows the NGO definition set forth in the Article 2.3 of the Law on the Development of Non-Governmental Organizations).

2. The applicant is a legal entity registered in the Republic of Lithuania for at least one year, i.e., no later than 06/10/2024.

3. The applicant's activities do not conflict with EU values and actively contribute (or seek to contribute) to the promotion of the following EU values and fundamental rights.

4. During the last three years (2022, 2023 and 2024) or since the establishment of the NGO, the applicant's average annual expenses were no more than EUR 300,000.

5. The applicant has submitted financial and annual activity reports to the National Center of Registers for the years 2022, 2023 and 2024, or since the establishment of the NGO.

6. The Open Lithuania Foundation is not a shareholder of the applicant.

7. Over the past three years (2023, 2024 and 2025), the applicant has not completed the Open Lithuania Foundation’s organized long-term capacity building program.

CSOs from all regions of Lithuanian are eligible to apply, except for CSOs that operate exclusively in the cities of Vilnius and Kaunas.

Both stages of evaluation of the applications will consist of administrative checks and quality assessment of the applications by independent experts. The quality assessment of applications will consist of the following stages:

•Expert evaluation.

•Review of applications by the Selection Committee and decision on funding.

Live information seminars will be held for potential applicants in 5 regions in Lithuania.

title: Framework partnership agreements to support EU level Networks active in the area: "Rights of persons with disabilities"
callTitle: Framework partnership agreements to support EU level Networks active in the area: "Rights of persons with disabilities"
descriptionByte:
Objective:

    • Promoting, protecting and monitoring the rights of persons with disabilities by providing financial support to EU-level networks of civil society organisations active in this area at local, regional, national and transnational level. It will in particular contribute to the implementation of the European Pillar of Social Rights (EPSR), the European Strategy for the Rights of Persons with Disabilities 2021-2030 (ESRPD) and the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD);
    • Supporting the Commission in putting the Strategy for the Rights of Persons with Disabilities 2021-2030 into practice;
    • Delivering on the European Pillar of Social Rights and related initiatives such as the ESRPD is a shared responsibility of the EU institutions, national, regional and local authorities, social partners and civil society. Civil society organisations are expected to:
  2. support its implementation at EU, national and local level notably by collecting and exchanging data and good practices and cooperating with public authorities in the design and implementation of relevant policies; implementing different mutual learning activities on concrete policies (mutual learning event/peer learning and other similar activities);
  3. organise communication and engagement activities to raise awareness of the ESRPD and promote the rights of persons with disabilities in Europe;
    • The ultimate goal is to build a stronger social Europe and ensure that people with disabilities can fully enjoy their rights.

results.summary: Journalism Science Alliance - call 1
results.content: Journalism Science Alliance - call 1

beneficiaryAdministration:
The Journalism Science Alliance (JSA) is a programme co-funded by the EU's Creative Europe Programme. JSA delivers grant funding, training, mentoring and networking to drive the production of local, regional, and transnational investigative journalism backed by science, and enhance cross-sectoral collaboration between journalism and research institutions. Supported by training and mentorship provided by JSA, journalists and scientists will work together to uncover new topics of public interest that will reach and engage (new) audiences for investigative journalism, while serving public interest across Europe.

The Journalism Science Alliance is managed by a consortium led by NOVA University Lisbon, in partnership with the European Journalism Centre (EJC).

Eligibility to apply

The grants will be open to:

  1. Collaborations involving at least one media outlet and one research/academic organisation working on an investigation on a topic of public interest, such as climate change, healthcare, emerging technologies, local governance, etc. The list of examples is not exhaustive.
  2. Organisations need to be based in one or more countries that have signed up to the full cross-sectoral strand of the European Union’s Creative Europe Programme, which provides core funding for the JSA.

Eligible countries include all 27 EU member states and the following non-EU countries: Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Norway, Serbia and Ukraine.

  1. The lead applicant is always a media outlet. The application should be submitted by a journalist associated with that media outlet who will act as the team lead. This can also be a freelancer, as long as they are supported by a media outlet.
  2. Individual journalists and/or scientists can be part of the applying teams as long as there are at least two organisations already involved in the application (1 media and 1 research organisation), but they cannot be lead applicant.
  3. Media, journalists, scientists, and/or research organisations from outside of the Creative Europe participating countries will be able to be part of the applying teams, as long as these already include one media and one research entity that satisfy the eligibility criteria.

Grant funding may be used to cover any costs necessary for the development, completion and publication of the research and production of journalistic content, including salary and human resource costs, research-related costs, translation and travel costs. The only exception applies to equipment (hardware) costs, which are not eligible. 

We are now launching the first Call within this programme. We are allocating approximately one million euro for supporting the first round of journalistic projects. Teams can apply for grants of 10,000 euro, 20,000 euro or 50,000 euro, depending on the scope of their project, the complexity of the proposed investigations, the number of partners involved, the nature of the associated tasks and the tentative timeline.

Selection process and timeline

The selection of successful applications is done by an independent jury made up of distinguished journalists and scientists.

Successful applicants will be notified about the outcome of their application as soon as the independent jury makes its decision. Given the expected high volume of applications, the Consortium reserves the right to not provide individual feedback to unsuccessful applicants. 

Grants are awarded for a period of 8 months. All funded projects must be finalised no later than the date specified in the grant agreement.

results.summary: Call for excellence scholarships for students of the Master's program AI & Health at Stockholm University
results.content: Call for excellence scholarships for students of the Master's program AI & Health at Stockholm University

beneficiaryAdministration:
Submission & Evaluation process

Purpose: Stockholm University is opening applications for scholarships aimed at supporting outstanding students enrolled in the Master’s program AI for Health, hosted by the Department of Computer and Systems Sciences (DSV) at Stockholm University (SU). The goal is to recognize and reward academic excellence and encourage students to make the most of their studies.

The hosting organism: the aim of the action is to motivate students enrolled in the Master’s program AI for Health to make the best out of their studies and support the most active and high-performing students. Awarded students will receive a grant to aid their educational journey.

The principles and procedure for awarding funding: this call is open only for students from EU-countries, EFTA countries, and those from countries already associated with the Digital Europe program (like Ukraine). Applicants need to be registered as students in the Master’s program AI for Health. Please note that this scholarship cannot be combined with other European-funded grants (e.g., the allowance awarded as part of the mobility for traineeship within the Programme Erasmus+) to avoid double-funding.

Applications:

Interested students must submit their application in English, including the following documents:

·A cover letter explaining the motivation for applying and how the grant would be used for (e.g., covering fees, travel for student exchanges, accommodation, living costs or other uses)

·A transcript of courses taken and the grades received per course so far per 2025-06-30

·Explanation for any missed courses or low grades

·Brief CV

·A copy of the applicant’s passport

Send the application via the submission box in the learning platform NextILearn.

Any questions regarding this call should be addressed to senior lecturer Ioanna Miliou <ioanna.miliou@dsv.su.se>

Selection criteria: grants will be awarded based on academic excellence, considering the number of courses and credits completed, grades achieved, and the strength of the motivation letter. (Example: a passed 7.5 credits with grade E is equal to 7.5 points, grade D is equal to 10 points, C is equal to 12.5, B is equal to 15 points and finally, grade A is equal to 17.5 points).

In the event of a tie between applicants, preference will be given to those who provide a clear and compelling explanation of why they apply for this grant and how they intend to use the grant.

results.content: Recruitment cycle Cohort 2025 – Call 2

beneficiaryAdministration:
This call is a follow-up to the "Recruitment cycle Cohort 2025" call, for the same SPECTRO Master's programme.

About SPECTRO

SPecialised Education programmes in CybersecuriTy and Robotics (SPECTRO) delivers two double-degree master’s programmes (ISCED Level 7, 120 ECTS) in two key digital technology areas for the future of Europe:

  1. Cybersecurity: this master's programme is designed to give students a general overview of the role that cybersecurity plays in creating a safe and inclusive digital society. It also equips them with practical skills in ethical hacking, blockchain technologies, and quantum cryptography.
  2. Robotics: the master's programme is designed to approach autonomous systems from both a computer science and an electronic engineering perspective. It covers everything from the basics of autonomous systems to such specific skills as: Internet of Things (IoT), Machine learning, Artificial intelligence, and Robotics.

The two specialised master’s programmes, also include a minor in Innovation and Entrepreneurship, are designed and delivered by a consortium consisting of 12 higher education institutions from 7 different countries, 2 innovative SMEs, 1 leading research centre in Information Systems and EIT Digital, a pan-European organisation with in-depth knowledge and experience in the digital skills domain.

About the scholarships

SPECTRO provides eligible students the financial support to take part to the education programmes and offers scholarship programmes to promote diversity in terms of gender, age, social and economic background. SPECTRO’s scholarships allow the greatest number to have access to high-quality education in digital areas and increase diversity among students and future digital experts.

The students awarded a scholarship will be financially supported during their two years of studies in one of the double-degree in Masters’ programmes offered by SPECTRO.

Types of scholarships available

These types of scholarships are available: full tuition fee waivers

How to apply

To apply to a SPECTRO scholarship, candidates must enrol into one of SPECTRO two master’s programmes.

Enrolment is done via a single application portal. When enrolling to one of the two master’s programmes, applicants are given the opportunity to select 3 options as Entry University and 3 options as Exit University with order of priority. It gives students a wider choice: applicants who would not be accepted to their preferred education institution might still be accepted by another education institution. At the same time, as the capacity of each education institution is limited, the multiple-option offer ensures that a high number of applications is processed.

To apply to the two SPECTRO Master’s programme, candidates are required to upload into the application portal the following documentation:

  1. Degree Certificate/Diploma in its original language and translated into English (If your university does not provide this service, the translation has to be done by an authorised translator and his/her credentials, signature and stamps must be visible in the translated document). In case of ongoing studies, a statement certifying that you are in the final year of your studies. The statement must be written by the degree administration office (or equivalent department) confirming that you are enrolled on the final year of your education and giving your expected completion date. Note: If applying to Aalto as entry, your bachelor degree must be completed by July 31, 2025.
  2. Official and stamped transcript of records in original language and translated into English. All courses taken must be included. Please scan the front and back of every document- all stamps and signatures must be fully visible.
  3. Proof of English proficiency. The requirement of English proficiency will vary depending on the higher education institution/country selected by the applicant. Please refer to EITD Master School website ‘Admissions’ tab for more information.
  4. Curriculum Vitae including details on your academic and professional career.
  5. A letter of motivation (maximum 3 pages) to prove the innovative potential of the applicant and their need for financial support. In this letter applicants will be required to discuss and/or propose an entrepreneurial idea and to explain their financial situation and need for financial support.
  6. Supporting documents regarding the applicant’s financial situation (e.g. credit report).
  7. An official ID, such as passport or National ID.

The allocation of scholarships will be done at the end of the selection process and before sending the letter of acceptance.

Eligibility requirements

SPECTRO scholarships are available to nationals of one of the eligible countries:

  1. EU Member States (including overseas countries and territories (OCTs))
  2. Listed EEA countries and countries associated to the Digital Europe Programme (associated countries) or countries which are in ongoing negotiations for an association agreement and where the agreement enters into force before grant signature

Only students enrolled and accepted in one of SPECTRO Masters’ programme are eligible to financial support. When receiving their letter of acceptance and study offer, students will be notified of their scholarship allocation.

Selection criteria

The scholarships will award applicants based on merit. To quantify merit, a merit score (on a scale from 1 to 5, with 5 being the maximum) will be given to each applicant accepted to one of the master’s programmes. Three elements will be considered in assigning a merit score:

  1. previous academic and professional experience of an applicant,
  2. curriculum vitae, and
  3. letter of motivation, which also includes the motivation for an applicant to receive financial support.

The initial merit score value will be an average of the two merit scores assigned by the two Local Programme Coordinators accepting an applicant (the Local Coordinator at the Entry University and the Local Coordinator at the Exit University). The merit scores assigned by Local Programme Coordinators will be reviewed by Programme Leaders to ensure uniformity between the scores given by Local Programme Coordinators from different universities and different countries. A final meeting including the Programme Leaders, all Local Programme Coordinators and the Quality Assurance Manager of the SPECTRO project will be set at the end of each Recruitment Period to agree and deliberate on the final merit score of each applicant.

Promotion of diversity in terms of gender, social and economic background

The SPECTRO scholarship programme will thrive to promote diversity and inclusion through its scholarship opportunities:

  1. Priority will be given to female applicants from any EU country or EU-associated country. The scholarship programme for women will aim increase female participation in master’s programmes in Cybersecurity and Robotics.
  2. Priority will be given to applicants from RIS countries - included in the EIT Regional Innovation Scheme (RIS). The scholarship programme for participants from RIS countries is aimed to support the participation of students from countries with moderate or modest innovation score and with lower gross domestic product. Countries eligible to take part to the RIS include 1) EU members states, 2) Horizon Europe associated countries, and 3) outermost regions such as Guadeloupe, and Réunion (France), the Azores and Madeira (Portugal), and the Canary Islands (Spain).

Payment arrangements

The scholarship is reflected as a discount in the tuition fee. The candidates are informed of the net amount of the tuition fee, after deducting the applicable amount of the scholarship.

  1. full tuition fee waivers: the nominal value of the granted scholarship is of 5,000EUR per year

The students awarded a scholarship will be financially supported during their two years of studies.

Number of scholarships available

Scholarships will be allocated on a rolling basis, until all financial support schemes are exhausted for the current recruitment cycle. With this call SPECTRO will make available full waiver 3 scholarships to be distributed among the two Master’s programmes.

SPECTRO scholarships are available to nationals of one of the eligible countries:

  1. EU Member States (including overseas countries and territories (OCTs))
  2. Listed EEA countries and countries associated to the Digital Europe Programme (associated countries) or countries which are in ongoing negotiations for an association agreement and where the agreement enters into force before grant signature

Only students enrolled and accepted in one of SPECTRO Masters’ programme are eligible to financial support. When receiving their letter of acceptance and study offer, students will be notified of their scholarship allocation.

Selection criteria

The scholarships will award applicants based on merit. To quantify merit, a merit score (on a scale from 1 to 5, with 5 being the maximum) will be given to each applicant accepted to one of the master’s programmes. Three elements will be considered in assigning a merit score:

  1. previous academic and professional experience of an applicant,
  2. curriculum vitae, and
  3. letter of motivation, which also includes the motivation for an applicant to receive financial support.

The initial merit score value will be an average of the two merit scores assigned by the two Local Programme Coordinators accepting an applicant (the Local Coordinator at the Entry University and the Local Coordinator at the Exit University). Promotion of diversity in terms of gender, social and economic background

The SPECTRO scholarship programme will thrive to promote diversity and inclusion through its scholarship opportunities:

  1. Priority will be given to female applicants from any EU country or EU-associated country. The scholarship programme for women will aim increase female participation in master’s programmes in Cybersecurity and Robotics.
  2. Priority will be given to applicants from RIS countries - included in the EIT Regional Innovation Scheme (RIS). The scholarship programme for participants from RIS countries is aimed to support the participation of students from countries with moderate or modest innovation score and with lower gross domestic product. Countries eligible to take part to the RIS include 1) EU members states, 2) Horizon Europe associated countries, and 3) outermost regions such as Guadeloupe, and Réunion (France), the Azores and Madeira (Portugal), and the Canary Islands (Spain).

Payment arrangements

The scholarship is reflected as a discount in the tuition fee. The candidates are informed of the net amount of the tuition fee, after deducting the applicable amount of the scholarship.

  1. full tuition fee waivers: the nominal value of the granted scholarship is of 5,000EUR per year

The students awarded a scholarship will be financially supported during their two years of studies.

Number of scholarships available

Scholarships will be allocated on a rolling basis, until all financial support schemes are exhausted for the current recruitment cycle. With this call SPECTRO will make available full waiver 3 scholarships to be distributed among the two Master’s programmes.

beneficiaryAdministration:
DTU Open Call Offer

The DigiWind DTU Open Call presents an opportunity for students aspiring to pursue a master’s degree in fields related to the digitalisation of wind and energy systems. The call targets applicants for the following DTU MSc programmes:

  1. MSc in Wind Energy  
  2. MSc in Sustainable Energy Systems  
  3. MSc in Sustainable Energy Technologies 

Successful applicants will receive a tuition fee waiver worth €30,000, which covers the full costs for the entire two-year (120 ECTS) MSc program at DTU. Up to four (4) students are expected to receive this waiver. 

Selected candidates will be based at DTU Risø and Lyngby Campus in Denmark, where they will have access to both in-person teaching and flexible digital learning opportunities, fostering a dynamic and comprehensive educational experience. 

This Open Call is intended for new applicants seeking admission to DTU MSc programmes in Wind Energy and Sustainable Energy for the Spring 2026 intake. 

To be eligible for the fee waiver, applicants must first apply to one of the MSc programmes during the official application period of DTU, which runs from August 15th to September 15th, 2025. Only after submitting the MSc application can candidates apply for the DigiWind fee waiver, which will be open from August 15th to October 15th, 2025.  

Applicants profile 

The program is aimed at individuals with a Bachelor of Science in Engineering (BSc Eng), Bachelor of Engineering (BEng) or a Bachelor of Natural Science (BSc) degree obtained at an internationally recognized university/higher education institution and/or existing industry professionals who can contribute directly to the digitalisation of the renewable energy sector. A foundational knowledge in physics, math, and engineering principles is required. 

Preference will be given to applicants with a strong motivation to pursue a career in Wind and Energy Systems and those who demonstrate a solid academic background in these fields. 

  1. Academic/Professional Background: Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree, master's degree, and/or be an industry professional who can contribute directly to the digitalisation of the renewable energy sector. 
  2. Nationality: Applicants must be a passport holder of Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Türkiye, or Ukraine. 

Evaluation process  

Submission will be done EXCLUSIVELY via F6S platform. A full list of applicants will be drafted containing their basic information for statistical purposes and clarity (which will be also shared with the EC for transparency). 

Applications will be evaluated by Applications will be evaluated by a panel of three Academics/Researchers at DTU Wind and Energy Systems. For more information on the selection and evaluation process please refer to the Guidelines for Applicants. 

Results notification 

A ranked list of candidates will be prepared, and scholarships will be offered following the order of merit within one week of the closing of the DTU Open Call. Successful applicants must indicate their intention to take up the offer within five (5) business days. 

Note: Approval for admission to the MSc programme at DTU is subject to consideration by the relevant department and will be granted after a thorough review of the candidate's academic background and application materials. Admitted students will receive further instructions from the DTU Admission Office. 

Evaluation results will be compiled into an Evaluation Summary Report, which will be sent out to applicants. Depending on the evaluation outcome (acceptance or rejection), applicants will receive via email:  

  1. Acceptance 
  2. An Evaluation Summary Report (ESR). 
  3. A Waiver letter offer and an invitation to the enrolment phase and following steps. 
  4. Rejection 
  5. An Evaluation Summary Report (ESR) for eligible applications that reached the internal evaluation phase. 
  6. A rejection letter to ineligible applications. 

 For more details, please refer to the Guidelines for Applicants. 

Redress process 

Applicants who are not satisfied with the evaluation of their application, may within 3 working days of the result being issued submit a written appeal, which will be reviewed by a panel, chaired by the DTU DigiWind representative, Project officer and one external member. Appeals are typically not allowed for disagreements with the academic judgment (score) or if the decision was based on the applicants misunderstanding of the application. Valid grounds for appealing a fee waiver offer decision generally focus on errors in the assessment process or claims of discrimination.

The EMAI4EU scholarship programme will thrive to promote diversity and inclusion through its scholarship opportunities:

  1. Priority will be given to female applicants from any EU country or EU-associated country. The scholarship programme for women will aim increase female participation in master’s programmes.
  2. Priority will be given to applicants from RIS countries - included in the EIT Regional Innovation Scheme (RIS). The scholarship programme for participants from RIS countries is aimed to support the participation of students from countries with moderate or modest innovation score and with lower gross domestic product. Countries eligible to take part to the RIS include 1) EU members states, 2) Horizon Europe associated countries, and 3) outermost regions such as Guadeloupe, and Réunion (France), the Azores and Madeira (Portugal), and the Canary Islands (Spain).

  1. full tuition fee waivers: the nominal value of the granted scholarship is of 5,000EUR per year

The students awarded a scholarship will be financially supported during their two years of studies.

Scholarships will be allocated on a rolling basis, until all financial support schemes are exhausted for the current recruitment cycle. With this call EMAI4EU will make available 15 full waiver scholarships to be distributed.

beneficiaryAdministration:
This call is a follow-up to the "Recruitment cycle Cohort 2025" call, for the same RESCHIP4EU Master's programme.

About RESCHIP4EU

Reinforcing Skills in Chips Design for Europe (RESCHIP4EU) aims to support the excellence of EU higher education in embedded systems design. RESCHIP4EU will achieve this goal by designing and delivering a double-degree master’s programme (ISCED Level 7, 120 ECTS) in Embedded Systems Design with specialisations in safer, greener, and smarter embedded platforms and a minor in Innovation and Entrepreneurship. The master’s programme will be designed and delivered by 9 higher education institutions from 5 different countries, along with Semi.org, ST Microelectronics, an innovative SME, an ASBL, and EIT Digital, a pan-European organisation experienced in delivering advanced digital skills education across Europe. RESCHIP4EU will foster strong interactions between academia and industry, promote entrepreneurship, and strengthen the integration of the knowledge triangle.

The two specialised master’s programmes, also include a minor in Innovation and Entrepreneurship, are designed and delivered by a consortium consisting of 9 higher education institutions from 5 different countries, 2 SMEs (EITD, and EA), 1 corporate (ST), 1 AISBL (JA Europe), and 1 international organization (SEMI) from 4 different countries with in-depth knowledge and experience in the digital skills domain.

About the scholarships

RESCHIP4EU provides eligible students the financial support to take part to the education programmes and offers scholarship programmes to promote diversity in terms of gender, age, social and economic background. RESCHIP4EU’s scholarships allow the greatest number to have access to high-quality education in digital areas and increase diversity among students and future digital experts.

The students awarded a scholarship will be financially supported during their two years of studies in one of the double-degree in Masters’ programmes offered by RESCHIP4EU.

Types of scholarships available

These types of scholarships are available: full tuition fee waivers

How to apply

To apply to a RESCHIP4EU scholarship, candidates must enrol into one of RESCHIP4EU two master’s programmes.

Enrolment is done via a single application portal. When enrolling to one of the two master’s programmes, applicants are given the opportunity to select 3 options as Entry University and 3 options as Exit University with order of priority. It gives students a wider choice: applicants who would not be accepted to their preferred education institution might still be accepted by another education institution. At the same time, as the capacity of each education institution is limited, the multiple-option offer ensures that a high number of applications is processed.

To apply to the two RESCHIP4EU Master’s programme, candidates are required to upload into the application portal the following documentation:

  1. Degree Certificate/Diploma in its original language and translated into English (If your university does not provide this service, the translation has to be done by an authorised translator and his/her credentials, signature and stamps must be visible in the translated document). In case of ongoing studies, a statement certifying that you are in the final year of your studies. The statement must be written by the degree administration office (or equivalent department) confirming that you are enrolled on the final year of your education and giving your expected completion date. Note: If applying to Aalto as entry, your bachelor degree must be completed by July 31, 2025.
  2. Official and stamped transcript of records in original language and translated into English. All courses taken must be included. Please scan the front and back of every document- all stamps and signatures must be fully visible.
  3. Proof of English proficiency. The requirement of English proficiency will vary depending on the higher education institution/country selected by the applicant. Please refer to EITD Master School website ‘Admissions’ tab for more information.
  4. Curriculum Vitae including details on your academic and professional career.
  5. A letter of motivation (maximum 3 pages) to prove the innovative potential of the applicant and their need for financial support. In this letter applicants will be required to discuss and/or propose an entrepreneurial idea and to explain their financial situation and need for financial support.
  6. Supporting documents regarding the applicant’s financial situation (e.g. credit report).
  7. An official ID, such as passport or National ID.

The allocation of scholarships will be done at the end of the selection process and before sending the letter of acceptance.

Eligibility requirements

RESCHIP4EU scholarships are available to nationals or residents of one of the eligible countries:

  1. EU Member States (including overseas countries and territories (OCTs))
  2. Listed EEA countries and countries associated to the Digital Europe Programme (associated countries) or countries which are in ongoing negotiations for an association agreement and where the agreement enters into force before grant signature

Only students enrolled and accepted in one of RESCHIP4EU Masters’ programme are eligible to financial support. When receiving their letter of acceptance and study offer, students will be notified of their scholarship allocation.

Selection criteria

The scholarships will award applicants based on merit. To quantify merit, a merit score (on a scale from 1 to 5, with 5 being the maximum) will be given to each applicant accepted to one of the master’s programmes. Three elements will be considered in assigning a merit score:

  1. previous academic and professional experience of an applicant,
  2. curriculum vitae, and
  3. letter of motivation, which also includes the motivation for an applicant to receive financial support.

The initial merit score value will be an average of the two merit scores assigned by the two Local Programme Coordinators accepting an applicant (the Local Coordinator at the Entry University and the Local Coordinator at the Exit University). The merit scores assigned by Local Programme Coordinators will be reviewed by Programme Leaders to ensure uniformity between the scores given by Local Programme Coordinators from different universities and different countries. A final meeting including the Programme Leaders, all Local Programme Coordinators and the Quality Assurance Manager of the RESCHIP4EU project will be set at the end of each Recruitment Period to agree and deliberate on the final merit score of each applicant.

Promotion of diversity in terms of gender, social and economic background

The RESCHIP4EU scholarship programme will thrive to promote diversity and inclusion through its scholarship opportunities:

  1. Priority will be given to female applicants from any EU country or EU-associated country. The scholarship programme for women will aim increase female participation in master’s programmes in Chip Design.
  2. Priority will be given to applicants from RIS countries - included in the EIT Regional Innovation Scheme (RIS). The scholarship programme for participants from RIS countries is aimed to support the participation of students from countries with moderate or modest innovation score and with lower gross domestic product. Countries eligible to take part to the RIS include 1) EU members states, 2) Horizon Europe associated countries, and 3) outermost regions such as Guadeloupe, and Réunion (France), the Azores and Madeira (Portugal), and the Canary Islands (Spain).

Payment arrangements

The scholarship is reflected as a discount in the tuition fee. The candidates are informed of the net amount of the tuition fee, after deducting the applicable amount of the scholarship.

  1. full tuition fee waivers: the nominal value of the granted scholarship is of 5,000EUR per year

The students awarded a scholarship will be financially supported during their two years of studies.

Number of scholarships available

Scholarships will be allocated on a rolling basis, until all financial support schemes are exhausted for the current recruitment cycle. With this call RESCHIP4EU will make available 20 full waiver scholarships to be distributed among the two Master’s programmes.

About ACHIEVE

Cloud and Networking Infrastructure, with the emergence of new trends like High-Performance Computing (HPC), are pivotal in driving Europe's key policy objectives like the Green Deal and digital transformation. The project, Advanced Cloud and High-performance computing Education for a Valiant Europe (ACHIEVE) is designed to enhance the quality of EU higher education in the domain of IT infrastructures and in particular HPC which is used to solve several complex questions in computational and data-intensive sciences. It offers a comprehensive approach, covering aspects from cloud computing, network architecture, to the advanced skills on HPC systems and their applications in answering complex questions like the simulation and modelling of physical phenomena (such as climate change, energy production, drug design, global security, and materials design), the analysis of large data sets (such as those in genome sequencing, astronomical observation, and cybersecurity), and the intricate design of engineered products, such as airplanes.

ACHIEVE aims to implement a double-degree master's program (ISCED Level 7, 120 ECTS) focusing on Cloud and Networking Infrastructure with two specializations that align with the strategic development of advanced, green, and efficient HPC systems. Additionally, it includes a minor in Innovation and Entrepreneurship. This program will be collaboratively designed and delivered by eight higher education institutions from six different countries, in partnership with major industry associations and companies specializing in cloud computing and HPC, along with an innovative SME for educational program delivery, a non-profit association, and EIT Digital, a leader in advanced digital skills education in Europe.

The specialised master’s programme, also includes a minor in Innovation and Entrepreneurship, are designed and delivered by a consortium consisting of 8 higher education institutions from 7 different countries, 2 innovative SMEs, 2 large enterprises, 3 leading research centre in Information Systems and EIT Digital, a pan-European organisation with in-depth knowledge and experience in the digital skills domain.

About the scholarships

ACHIEVE provides eligible students the financial support to take part to the education programmes and offers scholarship programmes to promote diversity in terms of gender, age, social and economic background. ACHIEVE’s scholarships allow the greatest number to have access to high-quality education in digital areas and increase diversity among students and future digital experts.

The students awarded a scholarship will be financially supported during their two years of studies in one of the double-degree in Masters’ programmes offered by ACHIEVE.

Types of scholarships available

These types of scholarships are available: full tuition fee waivers,

The monthly allowance will be weighted based on the country correction coefficient (CCCs) of the country where a student is studying. Thus, the monthly allowance provided to a student it can vary between the first and second year of studies.

How to apply

To apply to a ACHIEVE scholarship, candidates must enrol into one of ACHIEVE master’s programme.

Enrolment is done via a single application portal. When enrolling to one of the two master’s programmes, applicants are given the opportunity to select 3 options as Entry University and 3 options as Exit University with order of priority. It gives students a wider choice: applicants who would not be accepted to their preferred education institution might still be accepted by another education institution. At the same time, as the capacity of each education institution is limited, the multiple-option offer ensures that a high number of applications is processed.

To apply to one of the two ACHIEVE Master’s programme, candidates are required to upload into the application portal the following documentation:

  1. Degree Certificate/Diploma in its original language and translated into English (If your university does not provide this service, the translation has to be done by an authorised translator and his/her credentials, signature and stamps must be visible in the translated document). In case of ongoing studies, a statement certifying that you are in the final year of your studies. The statement must be written by the degree administration office (or equivalent department) confirming that you are enrolled on the final year of your education and giving your expected completion date. Note: If applying to Aalto as entry, your bachelor degree must be completed by July 31, 2025.
  2. Official and stamped transcript of records in original language and translated into English. All courses taken must be included. Please scan the front and back of every document- all stamps and signatures must be fully visible.
  3. Proof of English proficiency. The requirement of English proficiency will vary depending on the higher education institution/country selected by the applicant. Please refer to EITD Master School website ‘Admissions’ tab for more information.
  4. Curriculum Vitae including details on your academic and professional career.
  5. A letter of motivation (maximum 3 pages) to prove the innovative potential of the applicant and their need for financial support. In this letter applicants will be required to discuss and/or propose an entrepreneurial idea and to explain their financial situation and need for financial support.
  6. Supporting documents regarding the applicant’s financial situation (e.g. credit report).
  7. An official ID, such as passport or National ID.

The allocation of scholarships will be done at the end of the selection process and before sending the letter of acceptance.

Eligibility requirements

ACHIEVE scholarships are available to nationals of one of the eligible countries:

  1. EU Member States (including overseas countries and territories (OCTs))
  2. Listed EEA countries and countries associated to the Digital Europe Programme (associated countries) or countries which are in ongoing negotiations for an association agreement and where the agreement enters into force before grant signature and scholarship acceptance signature.

Only students enrolled and accepted in one of ACHIEVE Masters’ programme are eligible to financial support. When receiving their letter of acceptance and study offer, students will be notified of their scholarship allocation.

Selection criteria

The scholarships will award applicants based on merit. To quantify merit, a merit score (on a scale from 1 to 5, with 5 being the maximum) will be given to each applicant accepted to one of the master’s programmes. Three elements will be considered in assigning a merit score:

  1. previous academic and professional experience of an applicant,
  2. curriculum vitae, and
  3. letter of motivation, which also includes the motivation for an applicant to receive financial support.

(1) This criterion assesses the applicant's relevant academic achievements (GPA, degrees earned, relevant coursework, etc.) and any related professional experience. Higher scores will be awarded for stronger academic records, significant relevant experience, and demonstrable achievements. (2) This criterion evaluates the completeness, relevance, and quality of the submitted curriculum vitae. Higher scores will be awarded for CVs that are well-organized, clearly highlight relevant skills and experience, and demonstrate a strong career trajectory. (3) This criterion assesses the clarity, coherence, and persuasiveness of the applicant's explanation of their need for financial assistance. Higher scores will be given for statements that effectively communicate the applicant's financial situation and demonstrate a compelling need for support.

The initial merit score value will be an average of the two merit scores assigned by the two Local Programme Coordinators accepting an applicant (the Local Coordinator at the Entry University and the Local Coordinator at the Exit University). The merit scores assigned by Local Programme Coordinators will be reviewed by Programme Leaders to ensure uniformity between the scores given by Local Programme Coordinators from different universities and different countries. A final meeting including the Programme Leaders, all Local Programme Coordinators and the Quality Assurance Manager of the ACHIEVE project will be set at the end of each Recruitment Period to agree and deliberate on the final merit score of each applicant.

Promotion of diversity in terms of gender, social and economic background

The ACHIEVE scholarship programme will thrive to promote diversity and inclusion through its scholarship opportunities:

  1. Priority will be given to female applicants from any EU country or EU-associated country. The scholarship programme for women will aim increase female participation in master’s programmes in Cloud and Networking Infrastructure.
  2. Priority will be given to applicants from RIS countries - included in the EIT Regional Innovation Scheme (RIS). The scholarship programme for participants from RIS countries is aimed to support the participation of students from countries with moderate or modest innovation score and with lower gross domestic product. Countries eligible to take part to the RIS include 1) EU members states, 2) Horizon Europe associated countries, and 3) outermost regions such as Guadeloupe, and Réunion (France), the Azores and Madeira (Portugal), and the Canary Islands (Spain).

Payment arrangements

The scholarship is reflected as a discount in the tuition fee. The candidates are informed of the net amount of the tuition fee, after deducting the applicable amount of the scholarship.

  1. full tuition fee waivers: the nominal value of the granted scholarship is of 5,000EUR per year

The students awarded a scholarship will be financially supported during their two years of studies.

Number of scholarships available

Scholarships will be allocated on a rolling basis, until all financial support schemes are exhausted for the current recruitment cycle. With this call ACHIEVE will make available 15 scholarships to be distributed among the two Master’s programmes.

Cloud and Networking Infrastructure, with the emergence of new trends like High-Performance Computing (HPC), are pivotal in driving Europe's key policy objectives like the Green Deal and digital transformation. The project, Advanced Cloud and High-performance computing Education for a Valiant Europe (ACHIEVE) is designed to enhance the quality of EU higher education in the domain of IT infrastructures and in particular HPC which is used to solve several complex questions in computational and data-intensive sciences. All interested applicants may submit their application at any time during the Call opening period through the form hosted by EUSurvey. Applicants shall complete the online application form and upload the supporting documents. Application forms must be filled out in English. To be considered admissible, an application must:

●Be submitted in the electronic submission system (above form) before the deadline stated in the Call

Evaluation process: Evaluation is divided into three stages: 1) Eligibility; 2) Quality of the proposal; and 3) Selection

1.Eligibility

EUN as the coordinator of the C4DD will evaluate applications against the minimum eligibility criteria. The eligibility criteria are specified in this call document in the section “eligibility criteria” above. Applicants who are not in compliance with the above eligibility criteria will be subject to rejection at this stage.

2.Quality of the proposal

Four representatives of C4DD consortium partners will evaluate each application. The evaluators will assess three areas (“evaluation criteria”). Each area will be scored on a scale of 0-5. Applicants must score at least 3 points for each evaluation criteria in order to be selected.

0         

Proposal fails to address the criteria

1

The topic is inadequately addressed, or there are serious weaknesses.

2

The proposal broadly addresses the criteria but there are serious weaknesses

3

The proposal addresses the criteria well, but a number of shortcomings are present

4

The proposal addresses the criteria well with few shortcomings

5

The proposal successfully addresses all relevant aspects of the criteria

After evaluation by the selection panel, applications will be ranked, and the highest scorers will be eligible for funding. The maximum total score is 20 points. A minimum of 9/15 will be necessary to pass.

3.Selection

The evaluation scores by each team will be reviewed by the full project partnership where the selection criteria are applied (see the above section, “Selection criteria”), and the final decision is taken. This decision is then formally ratified by the project General Assembly to decide on the winners, who will then be invited to draw up a contract with the coordinator of the C4DD project.

All proposals will be informed about the evaluation result. Successful proposals will be invited for grant preparation; the other ones will be put on the reserve list or rejected.
description:
The outcomes of this FSTP call will vary depending on the status of the National Coalition applicants. The main distinction lies in Activity 1, as newly established NCs or those without a national website will be required to develop a new national website and connect it to the Digital Skills and Jobs Platform (DSJP). Existing NCs with operational websites will receive funding for the technical maintenance, upgrading, and security updates of their platforms. All National Coalition applicants must implement the activities outlined in Activity 2 and Activity 3 to ensure a cohesive and comprehensive approach to digital skills development across Europe.

In Activity 1: Web Development, new National Coalitions must develop a national website/database that will serve as a structured and coherent web antenna to the DSJP, providing content and data on digital skills and jobs in the official language(s) of their country. These websites must include interoperable links to the Core Platform, ensuring alignment with technical specifications. For NCs with existing national websites, the focus will be on upgrading, maintenance, and implementing security updates, ensuring continued functionality and reliability. 

Activity 2: Services, Content, and Community-Related Activities will require all NCs to develop and manage relevant digital skills content on their national websites. This includes presenting information about the National Coalition and its members, as well as curating and displaying relevant EU initiatives, funding opportunities, events, and training resources from the Core Platform. Each NC will implement an interoperable repository of good practices connected to the Core Platform and a repository of resources on digital skills, including strategies, training materials, case studies, and non-proprietary MOOCs. They will also highlight advanced digital skills training opportunities, ensuring accessibility across various learning formats and educational providers. 

To further support digital skills promotion, NCs will present funding opportunities at national and EU levels, publish relevant events in an online calendar, and produce news and skills intelligence reports to inform stakeholders about digital skills needs in their country. Additionally, they will organise webinars, online events, and peer-to-peer learning exchanges, contributing to the knowledge-sharing and community-building efforts of DSJP. Communication, promotion, and community management activities will also be a key focus, ensuring the visibility and engagement of stakeholders through press releases, newsletters, social media, and digital outreach strategies. 

Activity 3: Post-Editing and Localisation of Content will ensure that all National Coalitions translate and localise relevant content between English and their official language(s), making information accessible to national audiences while also sharing valuable national insights with the wider European digital skills community. This includes translating and reviewing EU policy information, skills intelligence, best practices, funding and training opportunities, news, and events. To facilitate efficient translation, NCs will have access to the European Commission’s translation system (eTranslation), with the responsibility of reviewing and refining machine-generated translations before publication results.  

Concrete actions 

More concretely the objectives stated above will be addressed via a number of concrete actions. National Coalitions websites are a gateway to variety of opportunities to empower citizens and organisation into their digital transition by offering relevant training opportunities, news, events, expert articles, etc to support skilling and upskilling. In particular, with regard to the outputs published on the National Coalitions websites, every National Coalition will meet the following KPIs: 

  1. Launch a national website and connect it to the Digital Skills and Jobs Platform (for newly established National Coalitions).  
  2. Presentation of the National Coalition and its members/activities in 4 categories 
  3. Overview of relevant national and regional strategies with description 
  4. Overview of EU initiatives and programmes in digital skills and jobs, relevant news and events 
  5. Presentation of 20 good practices from the national/regional/local level, with in depth 
  6. Presentation of 3 good practices 
  7. Presentation of 8 good practices from the Core Platform published on the national website 
  8. Presentation of 10 resources on digital skills 
  9. Presentation of 50 training opportunities targeting different groups of end- users 
  10. Presentation of 10 national and international financing opportunities in the field of digital skills 
  11. Publication of at least 20 relevant events in the calendar 
  12. Publication of at least 3 original news/announcements per month 
  13. Publication of at least 3 news/announcements per month transferred from the Core Platform 
  14. Publication and distribution of 2 original press releases per year 
  15. Organisation of at least 2 events, reaching on average 50 participants per event 

Each National Coalition will use the e-Translation tool on the Core Platform to translate content from their national website and publish it on the Core Platform. 

Each National Coalition must contribute at least 45 content items to the Core Platform. 

Additionally, each National Coalition must pull and translate at least 120 content items from the Core Platform to publish on their national website

callTitle: Champions for the Digital Decade Financial Support to Third Parties
furtherInformation:
The FSTP mechanism will provide targeted financial assistance to National Coalitions—both newly formed and existing—to support the implementation of activities outlined in this call. National Coalitions are multi-stakeholder partnerships that bring together a diverse range of actors—including ICT and ICT-intensive companies, training providers, education and employment ministries, public and private employment services, and civil society organisations—with the aim of developing concrete measures to deliver digital skills at every level of society within their countries.

For new National Coalitions, this includes their establishment and the development of national websites that are seamlessly integrated with the Core Platform and interoperable with national, regional, and local stakeholders. For existing National Coalitions with websites already funded under the CEF-TC 2019–2020 calls, FSTP will support the upgrading and maintenance of digital infrastructure, enhancement of data exchange capabilities, and improved usability and accessibility to foster greater stakeholder engagement and content dissemination. 

The allocation of FSTP will be based on the scope and scale of activities to be performed by each NC. This mechanism will play a crucial role in strengthening the overall network of NCs, fostering collaboration and ensuring effective skills development across all participating countries.

The completed application form shall be signed by the statutory body by means of a qualified electronic signature or a qualified electronic signature with a mandate certificate or a qualified electronic seal.

The applicant shall send the signed application form to the Authority in electronic form as an attachment to the electronic submission via the Authority's electronic mailbox established within the Central Portal of Public Administration www.slovensko.sk via the 'General Agenda' service.

An application that is not received by the Authority in the above-mentioned form will not be deemed to have been submitted and will be excluded from the evaluation process.

For more details on how to deliver the application, please refer to Annex 2 of the call for proposals, Conditions for the granting of GRANTs.

In order to establish the ranking of applications, each grant application is assessed with the application of the Criteria for the selection of projects, which form Annex 4 to the call . By applying the criteria for selecting projects, the Authority creates a descending ranking of applicants whose grant applications met the conditions for granting a grant, starting from the application that obtained the most points based on the criteria.

The purpose of applying the criteria for selecting projects is to determine the ranking of applicants, according to which the Authority sends a notification of compliance with the conditions for granting a grant. At the same time, it immediately sends the draft grant agreement to those applicants (in the order determined based on the project selection criteria) for whom the grant is fully covered by the amount of call funds available.

For applicants for whom the grant is not fully covered by the amount of available allocation of the call funds, the Authority will not send a draft grant agreement due to the lack of funds intended for exhaustion within the call.

beneficiaryAdministration: Proposals will be submitted electronically. Eligibility checks will be performed by representatives of the EUDOROS Consortium. Each eligible proposal will be evaluated across 3 criteria, namely Relevance, Impact and Implementation, by two external experts, and if their evaluations differ significantly a third external evaluator will be assigned to the proposal.
